take_homes: Name a framework the model already knows, tune it for my case, and ask the agent to run it, instead of writing the questions myself.
The agent's check of its own work is soft. A fresh reader with only the output, or me with my domain knowledge, is the real check. I skip checks too often.
Specific input like a concrete hate list beats vague categories. Vague input gets me the statistical-average version.

monday.move: Add a cold-reader step (fresh session, only the output as context) to one of our agent pipelines, then try the hate-list inversion on a team rules file.

monday.stop_condition: if the cold read finds nothing the original run missed on three outputs, drop it
monday.blocker: I'd rather build the bigger org-wide setup for the non-engineers first, so the check step will probably slip.

misconception.why: The point that the agent's self-report goes easy on its own output matched what I did when I skipped the review because it looked fine. I still think most checking is for beginners, but I accept it's a real failure mode at scale.

one_line: Good for people new to agents; I knew the context part, but the look-back going easy on itself and the cold reader were worth the day.
